title: Joshua 16:1–4
context: The second major allotment goes to the children of Joseph, the two tribes descended from Joseph's sons Manasseh and Ephraim. These verses trace the southern boundary of Joseph's combined territory in the central hill country, from the Jordan near Jericho, up past Bethel, and west to Gezer and the sea.

verses.text: The lot came out for the children of Joseph from the Jordan at Jericho, at the waters of Jericho on the east, even the wilderness, going up from Jericho through the hill country to Bethel.
verses.arminianNotes: "The lot came out for the children of Joseph." Arminian readers see the lot as God's chosen means of distribution, with Joseph's tribes called to receive their portion gratefully and live in it faithfully.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers recall that "its every decision is from the LORD" (Proverbs 16:33). Joseph's portion in the fertile central hills is God's appointment, fulfilling Jacob's blessings on Joseph's line (Genesis 48–49).

verses.text: It went out from Bethel to Luz, and passed along to the border of the Archites to Ataroth;
verses.arminianNotes: The boundary runs "from Bethel to Luz." Genesis 28:19 says Bethel's earlier name was Luz, so the relation between the two names here is debated. Arminian readers leave the question open and note Bethel's link to Jacob's encounter with God.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers also note the Bethel and Luz question without forcing an answer. They see significance in Joseph's border passing the place where God renewed his covenant promise to Jacob (Genesis 28).

verses.text: and it went down westward to the border of the Japhletites, to the border of Beth Horon the lower, and on to Gezer; and ended at the sea.
verses.arminianNotes: The line runs west past Beth Horon the lower to Gezer and the sea. Arminian readers note that Gezer, named here as a boundary, is the very town Ephraim later fails to clear (verse 10), a warning already present in the map.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that God sets Joseph's border to include Gezer. His assignment stands even where possession lags, and 1 Kings 9:16 records that Gezer finally came under Israel's control in Solomon's day.

verses.text: The children of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, took their inheritance.
verses.arminianNotes: "The children of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, took their inheritance." Arminian readers stress the active verb: Joseph's tribes are not passive; they must take hold of what God gives through faithful action.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see in Joseph's double portion the fulfillment of Jacob adopting Joseph's sons (Genesis 48:5). God keeps the word spoken through the dying patriarch, granting Joseph two tribal inheritances.
